q: Which figure shows a dimmer switch?
n: Figure A is a dimmer switch, which varies the light output by controlling the voltage or current to the lamp. Source: Wiring device manufacturer literature; Philippine Electrical Code (switches).

q: Which figure shows a USB outlet?
n: Figure C is a receptacle with built-in USB charging ports. Source: Wiring device manufacturer literature.

q: Which figure shows a range outlet?
n: Figure B is a range outlet: a heavy-duty, high-amperage receptacle for electric ranges, rated about 30–50 A with a distinct plug pattern. Source: Philippine Electrical Code (receptacles); NEMA WD 6 configurations.

q: Which figure shows a multipurpose outlet?
n: Figure E is a multipurpose (universal) outlet that accepts several plug types. Source: Wiring device manufacturer literature.

q: Which figure shows a pop-up floor outlet?
n: Figure D is a pop-up floor outlet, flush with the floor when closed, for open-plan offices and conference tables. Source: Wiring device manufacturer literature.

q: What electrical component in Figure A houses circuit breakers or fuses to distribute power within a building?
n: A panelboard houses the circuit breakers or fuses that divide the feeder into branch circuits and protect them. Source: Philippine Electrical Code (panelboards).

q: What enclosure in Figure B is used to safely house electrical connections, typically rated by environmental protection standards?
n: Figure B is a NEMA-rated enclosure, rated by environmental protection (NEMA 1 indoor, 3R and 4 outdoor and watertight) for housing electrical connections. Source: NEMA 250 (enclosures for electrical equipment).

q: What device in Figure C automatically switches a load between two power sources, often used in backup power systems?
n: An automatic transfer switch senses loss of utility power, signals the generator to start and transfers the load to it, then switches back when utility power returns. Source: Philippine Electrical Code (emergency systems); NFPA 110.

q: What safety device in Figure D protects electrical circuits by stopping the current flow in case of overload or short circuit?
n: A circuit breaker automatically opens the circuit on overload or short circuit and can be reset. Source: Philippine Electrical Code (overcurrent protection).

q: What device in Figure E is designed to quickly cut power to prevent electric shock, typically used in wet areas?
n: A GFCI (ground-fault circuit interrupter) trips within milliseconds when it detects current leaking to ground (about 5 mA), preventing shock. It is required in wet areas. Source: Philippine Electrical Code (GFCI protection); UL 943.

q: What is image 1 that supports and stabilizes the generator?
n: Item 1 is the skid mount, the steel base frame that supports the generator set, stabilizes it and allows it to be moved and anchored. Source: Generator manufacturer literature; NFPA 110.

q: What is image 3 that supplies mechanical energy?
n: Item 3 is the engine (diesel or gas), which supplies the mechanical energy that turns the alternator. Source: Generator manufacturer literature.

q: What is image 5 that regulates the generator’s voltage output?
n: Item 5 is the automatic voltage regulator, which controls the alternator's excitation to keep the output voltage steady. Source: Generator manufacturer literature.

q: What is image 6 that produces the electrical output?
n: Item 6 is the alternator, which converts the engine's mechanical energy into electrical output. Source: Generator manufacturer literature.

q: Which type of conduit is permitted for use in electrical service entrances?
n: Rigid steel conduit (RSC) gives the highest mechanical protection, so it is used for service entrance conductors exposed to damage. Source: Philippine Electrical Code (services, raceways).

q: What is an ATS for in an electrical system?
o: A switch used with a standby generator
An emergency switch in fire alarms
A switch for elevators and conveyors
n: An ATS is used with a standby generator. It transfers the building load between the utility and the generator automatically. Source: Philippine Electrical Code (emergency and standby systems); NFPA 110.

q: When is the Certificate of Electrical Inspection (CEI) issued?
o: Before the utility installs the meter
After the utility installs the meter
Before the Building Official's final inspection
After the Building Official's final inspection
n: The Certificate of Electrical Inspection is issued by the local building official after inspecting the installation. The utility requires it before installing the meter and energizing the service. Source: NBC (PD 1096) IRR, electrical permit and CEI; Meralco service application requirements.

q: Which of the following companies supplies electrical products?
n: Schneider Electric is a major supplier of electrical distribution products: breakers, panelboards and switchgear. Philips, Osram and Fumaco are mainly lighting brands. Source: Schneider Electric company website.

q: Which type of electrical enclosures is designed for outdoor use?
n: NEMA-rated enclosures (e.g., NEMA 3R, 4 and 4X) are designed and tested for outdoor rain, dust and corrosion. Source: NEMA 250.

q: When a circuit is divided into two or more branches, each branch transmitting part of the current, what is each branch conductor called when taken separately?
n: When a circuit is divided into branches that each carry part of the current, the branches are in parallel, and each branch conductor is called a parallel conductor. Source: Electrical circuit fundamentals; Philippine Electrical Code (definitions).

q: Which of the following appliances does not require an individual branch circuit?
n: A countertop microwave can share a general-purpose small-appliance circuit. Ranges, pumps and air conditioners need individual branch circuits. Source: Philippine Electrical Code (branch circuits for appliances).

q: What is the standard power voltage supplied by MERALCO?
n: Meralco supplies residential customers at a nominal 230 V single-phase (often called 220 V). Source: Meralco service standards; Philippine Grid Code / Distribution Code.

q: What frequency does MERALCO supply to consumers?
n: The Philippine grid, including Meralco, operates at 60 Hz. Source: Philippine Grid Code; Meralco service standards.

q: In a string of bulbs wired in series, what happens if one bulb is removed?
o: Only the bulb before it goes out
Only bulbs after it go out
n: In a series string the current has only one path, so removing one bulb opens the circuit and all the bulbs go out. Source: Electrical circuit fundamentals.

q: What device detects ground faults and cuts power immediately to prevent shock?
n: A GFCI detects ground-fault leakage current and cuts power almost instantly, preventing shock. Breakers and fuses respond to overcurrent only. Source: Philippine Electrical Code (GFCI); UL 943.

q: What are the conductors from a main distribution center to the branch-circuit panels called?
n: Feeders are the conductors between the main service or distribution equipment and the branch-circuit panelboards. Source: Philippine Electrical Code (definitions).

q: What resists the flow of electricity?
n: An insulator has very high resistance and resists the flow of electricity, e.g. rubber, PVC, glass. Source: Electrical fundamentals.

q: What conductors run from the service equipment to distribution points in a building?
n: Feeders carry power from the service equipment to distribution points (panelboards) inside the building. Source: Philippine Electrical Code (definitions).

q: A valve controls water flow. What does the same job in an electrical circuit?
n: As a valve opens and closes water flow, a switch opens and closes the path of current in a circuit. Source: Electrical fundamentals.

q: What is the minimum wire size required for a service drop?
n: The service drop (overhead service conductors) must be at least 8 mm² copper for adequate mechanical strength and ampacity. Source: Philippine Electrical Code (services); Meralco service drop requirements.

q: What is the minimum wire size required for a 60-amp circuit breaker?
n: A 60 A breaker protects a conductor rated at least 60 A. 14 mm² THHN copper is the commonly specified size for a 60 A circuit. Source: Philippine Electrical Code (ampacity tables, overcurrent protection).

q: What is the ampacity requirement for a 6-kW multipoint water heater?
n: I = P ÷ V = 6,000 W ÷ 230 V ≈ 26 A. The next standard breaker and wire rating is 30 A. Source: Philippine Electrical Code (branch circuit sizing).

q: For a1-horsepower air conditioning unit (ACU), what should be the size of the wire or cable?
o: All of the above (depending on load and installation conditions)
n: A 1 HP window or split aircon draws about 5–7 A running with a higher start-up current, so it is commonly put on 3.5 mm² wire with a 20 A breaker on its own circuit. Source: Philippine Electrical Code (motor and air-conditioning circuits); manufacturer installation data.

q: What matters most when sizing wire for a circuit?
n: Wire is sized by ampacity, the current it can carry continuously without overheating, then checked for voltage drop on long runs. Source: Philippine Electrical Code (conductor ampacity).

q: Power was cut but restored right away by standby generators. What switched the source automatically?
n: An automatic transfer switch detects the outage, starts the generator and switches the load over within seconds, with no manual action. Source: Philippine Electrical Code (emergency systems); NFPA 110.

q: What do banks typically use to ensure a smooth transition to emergency power during an outage?
n: Banks use an ATS to transfer their load to standby generators automatically during outages, usually with UPS units bridging the few seconds for computers. Source: NFPA 110; Philippine Electrical Code (standby systems).

q: What is the main function of an automatic transfer switch?
o: Switching automatically from the utility to a standby generator
n: An ATS's main job is to switch the load automatically from the utility to the standby generator, and back. Source: NFPA 110; Philippine Electrical Code.

q: What is the main purpose of a UPS?
o: Temporary power during outages or until a generator starts
n: A UPS uses batteries to supply power instantly during an outage, bridging the gap until the generator starts or giving time for a safe shutdown. Source: IEC 62040 (UPS systems).

q: In manual emergency switching, what device connects the load to the alternate source?
n: A manual transfer switch (MTS) is operated by hand to connect the load to the alternate source (generator). Source: Philippine Electrical Code (transfer equipment).

q: THHN wire is used for 600 V AC distribution in dry and damp locations. THHN stands for:
n: THHN = Thermoplastic, High Heat-resistant (90°C), Nylon-coated, a 600 V building wire for dry and damp locations. Source: UL 83 (thermoplastic-insulated wires); Philippine Electrical Code.
